proposal.name: Wrap poster bounds within the header

plan.name: Wrap poster bounds within the header
plan.summary: Wrap the reader poster subtitle into as many lines as needed within its existing padding, using the final poster width and preserving the reader label, checked-state count, sorted bounds and middle-dot separators between items on each line. Break only between whole items; shorten an item that alone exceeds the available width with a Unicode-safe ellipsis, leaving its full literal text in the unchanged complete evidence image and reader data. Animated and still posters use identical subtitle layout, keep the title and exploration badge in place, and move all chart content, arrow labels, initial markers, replay paths and the legend down by the added header height while enlarging the canvas; posters whose subtitle already fits remain byte-for-byte unchanged. Extend internal/statechart/poster_test.go with wrapping regressions and document this presentation behavior in docs/statecharts.md under Posters, preserving the existing validation, deterministic rendering and evidence contracts of D-0364. The merger records the subtitle presentation decision for #785 as a refinement of D-0364; the plumbing build does not write decisions/.

tests.name: TestPosterWrapsWholeSubtitleItems785
tests.says: Seven or many bounds wrap in order onto readable lines within the existing padding, identically in animated and still posters, while fitting subtitles retain their original poster bytes.

tests.name: TestPosterWrappedHeaderMovesTheWholeDrawing785
tests.says: Extra subtitle lines move states, arrows, label pills, initial markers, the animated replay and legend together, grow the poster height, and leave its width, title and badge fixed.

tests.name: TestPosterOversizedItemKeepsCompleteEvidence785
tests.says: An individually oversized bound is shortened safely with an ellipsis on one subtitle line; neighboring bounds remain complete and ordered, and rendering preserves the full bound in the evidence image and reader record.

usage.summary: Created `plan.json` and three acceptance tests covering wrapping, layout shifts, oversized bounds, and unchanged fitting posters. The check passed: all three tests fail on the base code as required, and `repo/` remains unchanged.
